title: Global Credit Finance, Model Risk Officer, VP

Ensure proposed AI use cases are appropriately identified, documented, risk assessed, and submitted through applicable enterprise AI governance and approval processes before implementation or production use. Evaluate whether tools and solutions may be subject to multiple governance frameworks, including EUDT, AI, model risk, data, privacy, cybersecurity, third-party risk, and technology-development requirements, and coordinate the required reviews with the applicable subject-matter experts. Promote the responsible use of AI by ensuring that approved tools are used only for authorized purposes and that AI-assisted outputs receive human review, validation, and challenge appropriate to the use case and potential business impact. title: Senior Operational Risk Manager
description: Mercury is revolutionizing finance for startups by building a complete, user-friendly banking* stack. We prioritize creating a secure and seamless experience for entrepreneurs while upholding the highest standards of compliance and safety. In this role, you will own the day-to-day operation of Mercury's Operational Risk program. You will report to the Head of Operational Risk, within the Risk organization under the Chief Risk Officer, and partner closely with first-line risk teams, Compliance, Third-Party Risk, Information Security, and Internal Audit. You will run the centralized issues and events program, coordinate risk and control assessments with first line teams, and drive reporting that give leadership and the Board a clear view of operational risk. This is a builder role. Much of the program is being stood up now, and you will have the autonomy to shape how it operates as Mercury prepares to operate as a bank. *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC. As part of the journey, we would expect you to: Set the risk and control assessment standard. Review and challenge first-line RCMs; independently test design and operating effectiveness on critical processes and issue findings. Oversee the operational event program: challenge first-line root cause, ratings and fixes; trend events across the enterprise. Own the centralized issues management program across operational events, incidents, testing and regulatory findings, from intake and triage through remediation tracking, validation, and closure Define enterprise KRIs and thresholds for each L2, tied to risk appetite, and aggregate first-line metrics into Board reporting. Partner with 1LOD teams, InfoSec, Compliance and model risk owners to collect inputs, challenge assessments and make sure risks are raised early. Provide second-line review and concurrence on high-risk new activities. Write and maintain the ORM standards, procedures and templates that first-line teams execute against. Support regulatory examinations, audits, and charter readiness reviews There are lots of paths that could lead you to be successful in a role like this; we think the strongest candidates will have some of this experience: 8+ years in operational risk, compliance, or internal audit at a bank or a fintech partnered with a bank Hands-on ownership of an issues management or operational event program, including severity rating, escalation, and validation of remediation Experience administering a GRC platform (LogicGate, Archer, or similar), including workflow configuration and reporting Strong data skills: you turn raw issue and event data into trends leadership can act on Familiarity with interagency and OCC expectations for operational risk management You challenge constructively, with evidence, and keep strong relationships with the teams you oversee You find, prioritize, and execute key projects independently, balancing program build with daily operations Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities or special needs. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role. #LI-AR1 Total Rewards The total rewards package at Mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options/RSUs), and benefits. description: Playing an essential role in the U.S. economy, Fannie Mae is foundational to housing finance. Join Fannie Mae to grow your career and help people find a place to call home. You will partner with senior leaders and practitioners across Cybersecurity, Technology, Architecture, Engineering, Data, AI and Risk to identify and evaluate material cyber and technology risks before they are designed into the environment. You will translate complex technical conditions, emerging threats and incomplete evidence into clear risk positions that articulate the exposure, affected business capabilities, control effectiveness, uncertainty, accountable ownership and decisions required. The role requires deep technical credibility combined with enterprise risk judgment. You will evaluate architecture and engineering patterns, challenge security assumptions and control dependencies, identify systemic and emerging risks, and help leaders determine whether to proceed, proceed with conditions, redesign, remediate or formally accept risk. As a Principal, you will also serve as a senior integrator when risk crosses domains such as AI, cloud, identity, data, application security, cyber defense, resilience and third-party technology. You will help convert recurring exceptions and individual findings into reusable risk patterns, scalable control expectations, and enterprise-level actions. The Way You Will Make a Difference This Principal role will offer you the flexibility to make each day your own while working alongside people who care, so that you can deliver on the following responsibilities: Lead first-line risk analysis and credible challenges for material architecture, AI/GenAI, agentic AI, cloud and engineering decisions, translating technical complexity into clear enterprise risk positions and actionable decisions. Assess architecture and engineering risk early in the lifecycle, including security design, trust boundaries, threat scenarios, inherited controls, data flows, identity and privilege, APIs, cloud services, software supply chains and resilience dependencies. Provide senior risk challenge for AI systems and emerging AI architectures, including risks associated with model and data integrity, prompt injection, sensitive-data exposure, excessive agency, non-human identities, tool access, third-party models/components and agentic workflows. Evaluate control design and effectiveness using evidence, distinguishing implemented and effective controls from policies, activities, dashboards or assertions, and identifying where evidence or assurance remains insufficient. Develop reusable risk scenarios, assessment approaches and minimum evidence expectations for established and emerging technology patterns, reducing reliance on one-off reviews and enabling consistent risk decisions at scale. Interpret threat modeling and scenario analysis to identify credible failure modes, attack paths, concentration risks and business consequences across interconnected technology environments. Connect technical exposures to enterprise impact, including critical business services, sensitive data, operational resilience, regulatory obligations and strategic initiatives. Frame decision-ready recommendations for senior management, clearly articulating exposure, evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, conditions, accountable owners and the decision required. Identify systemic and emerging cyber risks by connecting signals across architecture reviews, risk assessments, incidents, issues, exceptions, audit findings, technology change and industry threat intelligence. Drive accountable remediation and sustainable risk reduction, challenging whether proposed corrective actions address root causes and validating that closure evidence demonstrates meaningful reduction in exposure. Partner across Cybersecurity, Technology, Engineering, Data, AI and Risk while maintaining independence of judgment and clear accountability boundaries. Serve as a senior technical risk integrator and mentor, raising the quality of risk reasoning, technical challenge and executive communication across the broader risk organization. title: Business Control Manager
description: About the Role We are hiring a Business Control Manager to join Chime's Compliance Business Control Management team. You will own the control strategy, business relationships, and results for the Membership, App and AI Experience, and Trust and Safety portfolios. Working with the Enterprise BCM Lead and business partners, you will translate new initiatives, existing business activities, regulatory requirements, incidents, and other changes into clear control outcomes and practical plans. This is an individual contributor role for someone who can move comfortably between strategy and delivery. You will assess current control coverage, lead material control decisions and implementation work within your portfolios, and ensure controls are validated, documented, and maintained. Business and control owners remain responsible for implementing and operating their controls; you will provide the structure, challenge, and partnership needed to produce durable results. You will also contribute across the Enterprise BCM team by supporting Enterprise work when priorities and capacity require it, and by helping identify shared exposure themes and common control approaches across portfolios. In This Role You Can Expect To Own the control strategy and coverage view for assigned portfolios, using business activities, regulatory requirements, existing controls, gaps, and dependencies to set priorities. Evaluate new initiatives and the existing environment through reviews of process or product changes, incidents, complaints, findings, and current control practices. Determine whether controls should be reused, enhanced, created, consolidated, or retired. Lead control design and implementation with business and control owners, establishing clear objectives, scope, ownership, evidence, exception handling, delivery plans, and closure criteria while keeping control ownership and operation with the business. Assess control readiness, coordinate owner attestations, and determine whether controls meet the agreed validation criteria. Arrange an independent reviewer when your involvement in implementation requires additional separation. Lead control responses to incidents, issues, complaints, and findings by connecting root causes to control gaps, establishing remediation expectations, and confirming affected controls are revalidated before closure. Maintain reliable control records and use coverage, implementation, validation, and exception data to identify recurring themes, recommend shared approaches, and communicate results and remaining exposure to leadership. Build strong relationships across business, product, engineering, operations, legal, compliance, risk, and data teams, and support bank partner reviews, audits, examinations, and other assurance activities. To Thrive in This Role You Have 7 or more years of experience in business controls, regulatory compliance, operational risk, audit, or a related discipline within financial services, fintech, or another highly regulated environment. Experience independently owning a complex portfolio or control environment, setting priorities, leading cross-functional decisions, and moving work from assessment through validated and documented closure. Demonstrated ability to evaluate business activities and control coverage, distinguish control gaps from documentation or mapping gaps, and develop practical responses. Hands-on experience designing or enhancing controls with business, product, engineering, operations, or data teams and defining the evidence needed to demonstrate that controls operate as designed.
